_comment: Guided diagnostic procedures — each is a decision tree walked by GuidedProcedure state machine

PROC_HIGH_COOLANT_TEMP.title: Engine Overheating — High Coolant Temperature
PROC_HIGH_COOLANT_TEMP.warning: HOT SURFACES — Allow engine to cool before opening radiator cap. Risk of severe burns.

START.instruction: Park the vehicle safely and shut off the engine. Wait 5 minutes for initial cooling. Do NOT open the radiator cap yet.

CHECK_COOLANT_LEVEL.instruction: Check the coolant overflow reservoir level (do not open radiator cap). Is the coolant level at or above the MIN mark?

ADD_COOLANT.instruction: Top up the coolant reservoir with the correct coolant mixture (50/50 antifreeze/water). Check for visible leaks under the vehicle and at hose connections.

LEAK_CHECK.instruction: Are there visible coolant leaks (puddles under vehicle, wet hose connections, white residue at joints)?

ESCALATE_LEAK.instruction: Coolant leak detected. Vehicle must not be operated until the leak is repaired. Escalate to workshop for pressure test and leak repair.

CHECK_RADIATOR.instruction: Visually inspect the radiator fins for debris, bugs, or blockage. Are the radiator fins clean and unobstructed?

CLEAN_RADIATOR.instruction: Use compressed air or a soft brush to clean radiator fins from the engine side outward. Do not use high-pressure water directly on the fins.

CHECK_FAN.instruction: With the engine running at operating temperature, verify the cooling fan is engaging. Does the fan spin freely and engage when the engine is hot?

ESCALATE_FAN.instruction: Cooling fan failure suspected. Escalate to workshop to inspect fan clutch, fan drive, or electric fan motor and relay.

CHECK_THERMOSTAT.instruction: Using an infrared thermometer, check if the upper radiator hose gets hot within 5–10 minutes of running. Does the upper hose reach operating temperature (>75°C)?

ESCALATE_THERMOSTAT.instruction: Thermostat stuck closed — coolant is not flowing through the radiator. Escalate to workshop for thermostat replacement.

MONITOR_TEMP.instruction: Restart the engine and monitor coolant temperature for 10 minutes at idle. Clear the DTC and observe if it returns.

TEMP_STABLE.instruction: Did the coolant temperature stay below the warning threshold (98°C) during the 10-minute monitoring period?

ESCALATE_PUMP.instruction: Overheating persists after basic checks. Likely water pump failure or internal blockage. Do not operate vehicle. Escalate to workshop.

RESOLVED.instruction: Root cause identified and corrected. Coolant temperature is stable. Clear DTCs, complete a short road test, and monitor for recurrence.

PROC_LOW_OIL_PRESSURE.title: Low Engine Oil Pressure
PROC_LOW_OIL_PRESSURE.warning: CRITICAL — Continued operation with low oil pressure WILL cause engine damage. Shut down immediately if pressure does not recover.

START.instruction: IMMEDIATELY reduce engine load. If DTC is active while driving, safely pull over and shut off the engine within 30 seconds.

CHECK_OIL_LEVEL.instruction: Check the engine oil level on the dipstick with the engine OFF and vehicle on level ground. Is the oil level between MIN and MAX?

ADD_OIL.instruction: Add the correct grade engine oil (check door placard or owner manual) until the level reaches the MAX mark. Do not overfill.

CHECK_OIL_QUALITY.instruction: Inspect the oil on the dipstick. Is the oil clean (amber to dark brown) without a milky appearance (which indicates coolant contamination)?

ESCALATE_CONTAMINATION.instruction: Milky oil indicates coolant mixing with engine oil — likely a head gasket or oil cooler failure. Do NOT operate the engine. Escalate immediately.

RECHECK_PRESSURE.instruction: Start the engine and idle for 2 minutes. Observe the oil pressure gauge or monitor the DTC status.

PRESSURE_OK.instruction: Is the oil pressure now within the normal range (240–450 kPa at operating temperature) and the DTC cleared or inactive?

ESCALATE_PUMP.instruction: Oil pressure remains low despite correct oil level. Likely worn oil pump, blocked oil pickup, or bearing wear. Shut down immediately and escalate to workshop.

RESOLVED.instruction: Oil level was low — topped up and pressure restored. Monitor for oil consumption and check for leaks. Schedule oil analysis if consumption is high.

START.instruction: With the engine running at 1200+ RPM, measure battery voltage at the battery terminals with a multimeter.

CHECK_CHARGING_VOLTAGE.instruction: What is the measured battery voltage with the engine running?

ALTERNATOR_SUSPECT.instruction: Check alternator belt — is it present, tight (no more than 1cm deflection), and free of cracks?

TIGHTEN_BELT.instruction: Adjust or replace the alternator drive belt. Re-tension to the manufacturer spec. Restart and recheck voltage.

ESCALATE_ALTERNATOR.instruction: Alternator not charging with belt intact. Likely failed alternator or voltage regulator. Escalate to workshop.

ESCALATE_REGULATOR.instruction: Voltage above 15V indicates a failed voltage regulator overcharging the battery. This can damage electronics. Escalate immediately.

CHECK_CONNECTIONS.instruction: Alternator is charging correctly. Inspect battery terminals and cable connections for corrosion or looseness. Are all connections clean and tight?

CLEAN_CONNECTIONS.instruction: Clean battery terminals with a wire brush and baking soda solution. Tighten all cable connections. Apply anti-corrosion spray.

TEST_BATTERY.instruction: Perform a battery load test or check the battery age (typical lifespan 3–5 years). Does the battery hold voltage above 12.4V with the engine off?

REPLACE_BATTERY.instruction: Battery is failing and should be replaced. Escalate to workshop for battery replacement and charging system verification.

RESOLVED.instruction: Charging system is functioning correctly. Root cause was corroded/loose connections or a brief discharge event. Clear DTCs and monitor.

START.instruction: Check the fuel gauge — confirm there is sufficient fuel in the tank (above 1/8 tank). Low fuel can cause air ingestion and low pressure.

CHECK_FUEL_LEVEL.instruction: Is there more than 1/8 tank of fuel?

REFUEL.instruction: Refuel the vehicle. Prime the fuel system by cycling the ignition key ON/OFF three times without cranking, then start the engine.

CHECK_FUEL_FILTER.instruction: Check the fuel filter service interval (typically every 30,000 miles). Is the fuel filter within its service interval?

REPLACE_FILTER.instruction: Replace the primary fuel filter and water separator. Prime the system after replacement by cycling the ignition 3–4 times before cranking.

INSPECT_LINES.instruction: Inspect fuel supply lines from tank to engine for kinks, cracks, or loose fittings. Are all fuel lines intact with no air leaks?

ESCALATE_LINES.instruction: Fuel line damage or air leak found. Repair required before operating. Escalate to workshop.

ESCALATE_PUMP.instruction: Filter and lines are OK but pressure is still low. Likely a failing fuel lift pump. Escalate to workshop for pump replacement.

RECHECK_PRESSURE.instruction: Start the engine and monitor fuel pressure. Allow 2 minutes at idle for pressure to stabilize.

PRESSURE_STABLE.instruction: Is fuel delivery pressure now within the normal range (500–700 kPa)?

RESOLVED.instruction: Fuel pressure restored. Root cause was low fuel level or a clogged filter. Clear DTCs and monitor for recurrence.

PROC_CTS_SHORT_HIGH.title: Coolant Temp Sensor — Voltage High (Shorted to Power)

START.instruction: Turn the ignition OFF. Locate the Coolant Temperature Sensor (CTS) — typically on the engine block near the thermostat housing. Disconnect the sensor connector.

INSPECT_CONNECTOR.instruction: Visually inspect the CTS connector and wiring for damage, chafing, or bare wires contacting a voltage source. Is the wiring undamaged?

REPAIR_WIRING.instruction: Short to power confirmed by damaged wiring. Repair or replace the affected wiring harness section. Clear DTCs and verify repair.

MEASURE_RESISTANCE.instruction: With the sensor connector disconnected and ignition OFF, measure resistance across the CTS sensor terminals. A typical CTS reads 2–3 kΩ at room temperature.

RESISTANCE_OK.instruction: Is the CTS resistance within the expected range (approximately 2–3 kΩ at 20°C, decreasing with temperature)?

REPLACE_SENSOR.instruction: CTS sensor has failed internally. Replace the coolant temperature sensor. Clear DTCs and verify the signal returns to normal range.

ESCALATE_ECM.instruction: Sensor tests good but fault persists. Possible ECM pin fault or intermittent wiring issue. Escalate to workshop for harness continuity test and ECM diagnosis.

PROC_CTS_SHORT_LOW.title: Coolant Temp Sensor — Voltage Low (Open Circuit or Shorted to Ground)

START.instruction: Turn the ignition OFF. Locate the Coolant Temperature Sensor (CTS) connector. Disconnect it and inspect the connector for bent pins, corrosion, or moisture.

INSPECT_CONNECTOR.instruction: Is the connector free of corrosion, moisture, and bent/pushed-back pins?

CLEAN_CONNECTOR.instruction: Clean the connector with electrical contact cleaner. Straighten any bent pins. Reconnect and clear the DTC — verify if it returns.

FAULT_CLEARED.instruction: After cleaning and reconnecting, did the DTC clear and not return after a 5-minute idle?

MEASURE_RESISTANCE.instruction: With the connector disconnected, measure resistance across the CTS terminals. Also check continuity of the signal wire from the connector back to the ECM.

RESISTANCE_OK.instruction: Does the CTS sensor read approximately 2–3 kΩ at room temperature? Is there continuity in the signal wire?

REPLACE_SENSOR.instruction: CTS sensor is open-circuit or out of range — replace the sensor. Clear DTCs and verify signal is within normal range after replacement.

ESCALATE_ECM.instruction: Sensor and wiring test good. Possible intermittent fault or ECM issue. Escalate to workshop for further diagnosis with factory scan tool.

RESOLVED.instruction: Fault resolved by cleaning connector. Corrosion or moisture ingress was the root cause. Monitor for recurrence.

PROC_OIL_SENSOR_SHORT.title: Oil Pressure Sensor — Voltage High (Short to Power)

START.instruction: Turn ignition OFF. Locate the engine oil pressure sensor (typically on the engine block/oil filter housing). Disconnect the sensor connector.

INSPECT_WIRING.instruction: Inspect sensor wiring for chafing against hot or sharp surfaces, or bare wire contacting battery voltage. Is wiring undamaged?

REPAIR_WIRING.instruction: Wiring short to power confirmed. Repair or replace affected section of harness. Clear DTCs and verify.

TEST_SENSOR.instruction: With connector disconnected, use a multimeter to verify the sensor signal pin is not shorted to the reference voltage wire internally in the sensor.

SENSOR_OK.instruction: Is the sensor free of internal shorts (no continuity between signal and power pins with connector disconnected)?

REPLACE_SENSOR.instruction: Oil pressure sensor has failed with an internal short. Replace the sensor. Clear DTCs and verify normal operation.

ESCALATE_ECM.instruction: Sensor and wiring test normal. Possible ECM fault. Escalate to workshop for advanced diagnosis.

PROC_HIGH_BATTERY_VOLTAGE.title: Battery Voltage Above Normal (Overcharging)
PROC_HIGH_BATTERY_VOLTAGE.warning: Overcharging can damage the battery, electronics, and cause battery gassing. Resolve promptly.

START.instruction: With the engine running at 1200 RPM, measure voltage at the battery terminals with a multimeter.

CONFIRM_VOLTAGE.instruction: Is the measured battery voltage above 15.0V with the engine running?

CHECK_SENSOR.instruction: Voltage appears normal at the battery. The DTC may have been triggered by a momentary spike. Check the battery voltage sensor wiring and connections.

SENSOR_OK.instruction: Are the battery voltage sensor connections clean and tight?

CLEAN_FIX.instruction: Clean and tighten connections. Clear DTC and monitor. Likely a false trigger from a momentary connection issue.

ESCALATE_REGULATOR.instruction: Overcharging confirmed — voltage regulator or alternator failure. Do not operate vehicle until repaired. Escalate to workshop immediately.

RESOLVED.instruction: Charging voltage is within normal range. DTC was likely a transient event. Clear and monitor.
